requirement_text.REQ-425:
MOB-6 in docs/mobile/requirements.md (build-order M6; depends on M2). Built BEFORE MOB-4 (REQ-426..428) -- see the S9 header: the renderers' six states classify this requirement's ApiError. SECURITY-REVIEWER gate (refresh-token handling, token clearing).

Hardens lib/api/api_client.dart (created by REQ-421) into the single client:
1. Attach the active tenant's bearer token (REQ-422's iss check).
2. On 401: exactly one silent refresh via flutter_appauth's token refresh, then exactly one retry of the original request; concurrent 401s share one in-flight refresh. On refresh failure: clear the tenant's tokens (REQ-422 store) and route to login.
3. Exponential backoff on 5xx for idempotent methods only (GET), bounded attempts; POST is not auto-retried (no duplicate task completion).
4. Normalise every failure to a sealed ApiError type before it leaves lib/api/: at minimum network-unavailable, unauthorized, forbidden (403), not-found, module-not-available (a 404 on any /api/v1/modules/<id>/ path -- architecture.md §6: absence is 404, not 403, and must not render as a generic not-found), backpressure (429, carrying the Retry-After seconds -- the backend emits 429 from lib/letflow/plugs/admission.ex and lib/letflow/plugs/public_read_rate_limit.ex), validation (422 with RFC 9457 field errors), conflict (409), server (5xx after retries).
5. A static guard (apps/mobile/test/guards/), the counterpart of the SPA's raw-fetch-outside-client guard in web/tests/guards/: no file outside lib/api/ imports package:dio or package:http or uses dart:io HttpClient; with a self-test.

result.summary: Reviewed commit 298e8e84 (git show 298e8e84 -- apps/mobile/lib/definitions/pinned_form_resolver.dart apps/mobile/test/definitions/pinned_form_resolver_test.dart) against ApiClient.get's real contract in apps/mobile/lib/api/api_client.dart (_sendWithBackoff, lines ~465-511): the loop only ever `return response` when statusCode is 2xx (401 routes through _handleUnauthorized, which itself only returns on success or throws); every other status, and every DioException, ends in `throw classifyError(...)`. So `ApiClient.get()` can never return a Response with a non-2xx statusCode -- the removed `if (response.statusCode != 200)` branch was genuinely unreachable, confirming this is dead-code removal, not a behavior change. (1) No-behavior-change: PinnedFormResolved/PinnedFormUnavailable outcomes for all four input classes (cache-hit, cache-miss-fetch-success incl. null form_schema, cache-miss-fetch-exception, null-form-version) are unchanged -- both the old dead branch and the surviving catch(_) returned the identical PinnedFormUnavailable(fetchFailed), and the dio.Response import/local var removal is a pure type-narrowing cleanup with no logic change. (2) No scope creep: diff touches only pinned_form_resolver.dart (removed dio import, Response<dynamic> local -> dynamic, dead branch, doc-comment updates) and its own test file; nothing else in lib/definitions/ or beyond was touched. (3) Updated test genuinely exercises the real path: the AC3 404 case now does `_FakeGateway(errorToThrow: const NotFoundError())` and the resolver's own catch(_) block catches it via the same code path as the network-exception test, asserting the identical PinnedFormUnavailable(fetchFailed) outcome -- not a rubber-stamp, it reflects ApiClient's real throwing contract.
